title: Azure Data Factory Overview
description: Orchestrate data movement and transformation with Data Factory pipelines, linked services, datasets, and integration runtimes.

data.text: Azure Data Factory (ADF) is a managed orchestration service for data integration. You describe where data comes from (linked services and datasets), what to do with it (activities in a pipeline), and when to run it (triggers). Pipelines can copy data at scale, call a stored procedure, run a Databricks notebook, or fan out work with ForEach. Azure Synapse pipelines are the same engine inside a Synapse workspace.

data.caption: A pipeline chains activities that read datasets through linked services; triggers start runs on a schedule or when data arrives.
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    TRIG["Trigger\nschedule or event"] --> PL["Pipeline"]
    PL --> A1["Lookup: get watermark"]
    A1 --> A2["Copy: source to sink"]
    A2 --> A3["Stored procedure:\napply SCD logic"]
    LS1["Linked service: Blob"] --> A2
    LS2["Linked service: Azure SQL"] --> A2
    A3 --> MON["Monitor and alert"]

data.text: A Copy activity takes a source dataset and a sink dataset. The sink can upsert rows using the keys you declare, which is the usual pattern for a nightly incremental load.

data.title: Pipeline with a Copy activity
data.content: The activity copies a delimited file from Blob Storage into Azure SQL, upserting by OrderId so re-runs are safe.

data.title: Linked service for Blob Storage
data.content: In production, prefer a managed identity over an account key so no secret is stored in the factory.

data.title: Create and run with the Azure CLI
data.content: The `datafactory` commands create the factory, register the linked service and pipeline, and start a run.
data.code:
az datafactory factory create \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --name adf-demo \
  --location westeurope

az datafactory linked-service create \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --factory-name adf-demo \
  --name ls_blob \
  --properties @ls-blob.json

az datafactory pipeline create \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --factory-name adf-demo \
  --name pl_copy_orders \
  --pipeline @pl-copy.json

az datafactory pipeline create-run \
  --resource-group rg-demo \
  --factory-name adf-demo \
  --name pl_copy_orders

data.title: Interview angle: Data Factory vs SSIS vs custom code
data.text: Data Factory is the cloud-native orchestrator: it is serverless, scales out, integrates with Azure services, and monitors every run. SSIS is the on-premises and lift-and-shift option with a rich transformation surface. Custom code in Databricks or Functions wins when the transformation is complex or the volume is very large. A common answer is ADF for orchestration, Databricks or Synapse for transformation, and a warehouse for serving.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Data Factory orchestrates data movement and transformation across services.
Linked services define connections; datasets describe the data shape.
Pipelines chain activities such as Copy, Lookup, ForEach, and Stored Procedure.
Triggers start runs on a schedule, a tumbling window, or an event.
Integration runtimes provide the compute, including self-hosted runtimes for private networks.
Use managed identity instead of keys, and monitor runs with alerts.
